newsitem.title: CHINA: China group seeks tough moves on Japan over islands.
newsitem.headline: China group seeks tough moves on Japan over islands.

text.p: A group of Chinese activists announced the formation of an alliance to champion China's claim to the disputed Diaoyu islands on Sunday and called for the authorities to take tough measures against rival claimant Japan.
The organisers urged the Communist Party's powerful Central Military Commission to take a tough stance against what they called Tokyo's occupation of Chinese territory.
The move came as more than 3,000 people took to the streets of Hong Kong in protest at Tokyo's claims to the uninhabited islands in the South China Sea.
In Taiwan, which also disputes Tokyo's claim, angry residents formed a similar alliance and threatened to organise mass protests against Japan.
Japanese rightists have built a makeshift lighthouse on one of the Diaoyu islands, known as the Senkakus in Japanese.
The islands are about 300 km (190 miles) west of Okinawa and 200 km (125 miles) east of Taiwan.
The Chinese government has urged Tokyo not to do "anything foolish" over the islands and has expressed concern over what it sees as a rise in Japanese right-wing activity.
The unofficial Beijing group said it wanted to organise protest sailings to the islands.

It also said it planned a rally at the Japanese embassy in Beijing on September 18, the anniversary of a 1931 incident that China marks as the start of Japanese aggression that culminated in World War Two.
The group said in a brief statement that its main tasks included "to continue to urge the central military commission to take tough action against Japan's occupation of the Diaoyu islands".

One of the founders of the group is Tong Zeng, who has led an unofficial campaign for compensation from Japan on behalf of people who say that relatives were killed or abused during Tokyo's occupation of China in the 1930s and 1940s.
Tong told Reuters the group would act peacefully and within Chinese law.
"We are applying for permission from the police to stage our protest," he said.
